terms.grammar: verb (opīnor, opīnārī, opīnātus sum) set into the sentence, like English “I expect”
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 1.92: nōndum, opīnor, est experrēctus
Gell. 2.22.20: ā turbine, opīnor, ejus ac vertīgine
terms.comment: Latin has no everyday adverb for “probably”: it says what the speaker supposes, with opīnor, putō or crēdō set into the clause.

terms.gloss: I suppose, I dare say; often ironic
evidence: Plaut. Bacch. 106: nam utī nāvī vecta es, crēdō timida es
Plaut., Ter., Cic., Caes., Sall., Liv. (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Polite, modest or ironic (Lewis & Short): it can mean “no doubt” said with a smile.

evidence: Cic. Tusc. 2.5: id quod vērī simile occurrit (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 3.13.6: quod est magis vērī simile
terms.comment: Cicero writes it as two words; later it is often one, vērīsimile (Lewis & Short). As an adjective, of a story or an explanation: vērī similis, likely (M-O s.v. probable, likely; Traupman 340, vērīsimilis).

terms.gloss: it is most likely, very probably
terms.grammar: superlative of vērī simile est, with an accusative and infinitive
evidence: Cic. Inv. 1.4: vērī simillimum mihi vidētur (Lewis & Short s.v. vērus)
Traupman 340: vērī simillimum est eam ventūram esse
Cic. Att. 4.19.1: sed nisi fallor citius tē quam scrībis vidēbō
Cic. Or. 122: rem breviter expōnere et probābiliter (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short’s “probably” is the old English sense “credibly”: every classical example is of telling or arguing a thing convincingly, never “in all likelihood”.

evidence: Traupman 102, 340: most likely she will come, proximum est ut veniat
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: proximum est, ut, “it follows that, remains that, the next point is” (proximum est, ut doceam …, Cic. N.D. 2.73): a step in an argument, not a likelihood (see then, next). For “most likely” say vērī simillimum est (Cic. Inv. 1.4, Lewis & Short s.v. vērus), which is Traupman’s own second version.

phrases.english: he probably hasn’t woken up yet

phrases.latin: nam utī nāvī vecta es, crēdō timida es.
phrases.english: since you came by ship, you were probably frightened.

phrases.latin: sed nisi fallor citius tē quam scrībis vidēbō
phrases.english: but unless I’m mistaken I’ll see you sooner than you say

phrases.latin: etsī vix vērī simile est, mīsī tamen Puteolōs puerōs quī pervestīgārent
phrases.english: though it was hardly likely, I still sent slaves to Puteoli to track him down

phrases.latin: Vērī similius est (+ acc. and inf.)
